prompt:
Use the attached image as the primary visual style reference. Create a NEW small dungeon battle scene, not a collage. Match its coarse low-resolution pixel clusters, muted gray-green slab floors, dusty brown and mauve stone walls, deep purple-black void outside the rooms, dark understated outlines, tiny compact adventurer/monster sprites with oversized readable heads and short bodies, restrained cyan and warm ochre accents. Top-down three-quarter dungeon videogame view exactly in the spirit of the reference: square floor tiles, vertical back-wall faces, no floating isometric diamond board. Aim for the apparent chunky pixel scale of a 192x144 scene enlarged cleanly to a 4:3 image. No painterly brushwork, no smooth gradients, no antialiasing, no tiny texture noise, no modern vector symbols. Readable silhouettes and quiet walking space matter more than ornament. Props have broad simple shapes and stay mainly against walls. Six to eight tiny figures are spatially separated and readable, with a shield, bow, dagger, robed caster and monster silhouettes. No title, lettering, interface panels, health bars or decorative frame. Keep the reference's level of simplification and subdued contrast. Use a 4:3 composition.

VARIATION 3: A T-shaped underground chapel with a recessed upper alcove and a short broad stone altar. Empty central square, two thick wall piers framing the aisle, short broken benches pushed to the sides, a torn dark red cloth only in the alcove. Figures spread across the transverse aisle with a clear line of approach from below. Dusty violet-gray floor, desaturated reddish walls, tiny pale cyan highlights. Keep architecture low and floor readable.
